title: fix: notify owners of leaked publishable keys
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Shows a targeted dashboard notice only for keys marked `directUseDisabledDueToLeak`
- Distinguishes disabled direct-only keys from app keys whose direct Pollen spending is blocked
- Keeps Pollinations Auth (BYOP) available for protected app keys
- Uses the existing key metadata JSON, with no schema or endpoint changes

Checks:
- `npx biome check --write enter.pollinations.ai/frontend/src/components/keys/api-key-list.tsx`
- `npm run typecheck --workspace enter.pollinations.ai`
- `npm run build:frontend --workspace enter.pollinations.ai`

gist.headline: The keys get a heads-up
gist.blurb: Protected app keys now leave a small, useful note on the dashboard when direct use has been switched off. Polli believes mysterious key behavior belongs in the past, alongside unlabeled jars of honey.
gist.summary: The API key dashboard now shows a targeted notice for keys marked `directUseDisabledDueToLeak`, clearly distinguishing disabled direct-only keys from app keys that block direct Pollen spending while retaining Pollinations Auth (BYOP).
gist.impact: Key owners can now see why direct usage is unavailable and confirm that protected app keys can still use Pollinations Auth for their app flows.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Polli as a careful keykeeper in a cozy garden-workshop, placing a friendly notice card beside a protected golden API key on a retro terminal. The key has a small shield and a separate sign for direct use, while a blooming code-plant and an Auth pass indicate that protected app access still works.
gist.image_prompt: Cozy pixel art scene of Polli, the cute yellow-and-brown striped bee mascot with pink blush, light blue wings, and a tiny keykeeper hat, carefully attaching a friendly notice card to a golden pixel API key with a small shield beside a lime green (#ecf874) retro terminal; a separate glowing Auth pass and blooming code-plants show the app is still welcome. Cozy 8-bit pixel art aesthetic, soft pastel gradients, warm lighting, retro gaming vibes, with subtle pixel-font text: 'KEY NOTICE'.
